summary:
Allwork.Space reports on new payroll data from HR data firm Brightmine showing a persistent gender bonus gap in the United Kingdom. Based on payroll records for almost 1.46 million employees at 1,190 organizations as of July this year, men received average annual bonuses of GBP 5,442 (about $7,300) versus GBP 3,062 for women. The gap narrowed only slightly from a year earlier.

Additional findings: 14% of male employees received a bonus compared with 9% of female employees, while overall 13% of employees received a bonus, unchanged year over year. The disparity widened with age, with 56-year-old men receiving average bonuses of GBP 8,817 against GBP 3,769 for women of the same age. Some of the largest gaps appeared in finance and in professional and business services.

Sheila Attwood, HR insights and data lead at Brightmine, said the findings suggested differences in progression, seniority and access to higher-value incentive schemes rather than a single cause.

For context, Britain's Office for National Statistics estimated the overall gender pay gap at 6.9% in April last year, indicating the bonus gap is far wider proportionally than the headline pay gap.

The piece is a short newswire item (written by William Schomberg, edited by Andy Bruce) and does not address workplace operations topics such as office attendance, desk or room booking, visitor management or facilities. It is relevant to HR compensation and equity reporting rather than workplace technology.
